scope.evidence_basis: Author rereading and explicit calculation of the fixed-node argument, with source support scoped as recorded. Checked every exponent in K=C1*C0*T^(-1/p)*G+T^(1-1/q)*D. W11 yields continuous A1 representatives but cone membership is retained only almost everywhere. For bad times [v]>R, Markov gives measure<=T^(1-1/p)G/R and uniform A1 amplitude gives an L1 tail with the same small factor. Compact convex hulls of gauge-bounded value sets give all interval-integral compactness. For q=1 and finite p, bounded-amplitude interpolation supplies target Lp(A1) translations; for q>1 it supplies supremum translations. Simon yields weak-space precompactness, and the two-point inequality with eta chosen first upgrades to A0. At p=infinity the full-measure dense-time argument yields A0 continuous extensions if needed; the theorem itself only claims L-infinity compactness. The proof has no assumption that limits stay in the cone.

N-cone-mechanism: Derive the A1 supremum bound and control the gauge-truncation tail.
Obtain compact interval integrals and apply Simon using the correct derivative exponent.
